intro: A React single-page app on Netlify talks to a Spring Boot API on Render, backed by PostgreSQL on Neon. Portfolio content is versioned JSON in the repo; blog posts, comments and messages live in the database.

decisions.title: Portfolio content in JSON, blog content in PostgreSQL
decisions.body: Profile, skills, experience and projects change rarely and are versioned with the code in src/static-data. Blog posts and comments change often and need search, moderation and analytics, so they live behind the API.

decisions.title: Stateless JWT with Spring's OAuth2 resource server
decisions.body: Instead of a hand-rolled filter, tokens are HS256-signed with NimbusJwtEncoder and validated by the resource server. Roles travel in a "roles" claim and map to ROLE_ADMIN / ROLE_VISITOR authorities.

decisions.title: PostgreSQL full-text search before Elasticsearch
decisions.body: A generated, weighted tsvector column (title > summary > body) with a GIN index and websearch_to_tsquery covers search without another service to run.

decisions.title: Cache the read path only
decisions.body: Single posts, popular posts and the tag list are cached; any admin write evicts them. View counts are incremented with a direct UPDATE so they never invalidate the cache.

decisions.title: Spam protection without CAPTCHAs
decisions.body: Comments and the contact form use a hidden honeypot field plus per-IP sliding-window rate limits. Comments are held for moderation by default.

decisions.title: Flyway owns the schema
decisions.body: Hibernate runs with ddl-auto=validate, so the app refuses to start if entities and migrations drift. Integration tests run the real migrations on PostgreSQL via Testcontainers.

decisions.title: One origin in production
decisions.body: Netlify proxies /api to Render, so the browser only ever talks to one domain: no CORS preflights, no API URL baked into the build, and the backend can move without rebuilding the frontend.

decisions.title: Built to fit free tiers
decisions.body: The backend binds to $PORT, keeps a 5-connection pool for Neon, caps the JVM heap for a 512 MB instance, and can run without Redis, so the whole site runs at zero cost.
